title: Voice signal propulsion and feature ambit - Jan 2026
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of the last four weeks of incoming signals (support tickets, CSM interviews, NPS comments, and product analytics) with a compact feature-request catalogue and pragmatic probe suggestions. Goal is to produce a lightweight, prioritized set of actions that eng/product can take as 0–3 month probes and a companion set of low-effort customer mitigations.

Context and data sources:
- Triage window: 2025-12-01 to 2026-01-12.
- Sources: support tickets tagged "latency" or "inference-quirk", weekly CSM call notes (Dec/Jan), two enterprise customer interviews (healthcare, fintech), runtime trace snippets, and a set of 12 user-submitted reproductions.
- Sampling note: we prioritized tickets that included traces or reproducible payloads.

Topline synthesis (executive summary):
- Two recurring pain patterns drive ~55% of high-severity asks: 1) unpredictable tail latency on streaming responses when KV-cache misses coincide with users sending long prompt prefixes; 2) confusing behavior and cost surprises from caching + batching interactions (users see higher token counts than expected).
- Customers want clearer failure modes and deterministic fallbacks: explicit, actionable signals (not opaque 500s, not silent slowdowns).
- Several mid-market customers (finance/healthcare) require private deployment guidance for compliance but are blocked by unclear KMS + audit guidance.

Notable customer quotes (verbatim where possible):
- "We thought caching would reduce cost but sometimes it spikes—hard to tell why." — Fintech platform ops
- "When the model switches mid-request we lose context and the UX looks broken. Need a predictable fallback." — Internal tools PM (start-up)
- "Can you tell me which tokens are billed at what rate? The console shows a number but it doesn't map to our implementation." — Enterprise SRE

Patterns and root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) KB/Prefix cache rehydration occurs during heavy tail-load windows and coincides with loss of streaming pacing; hypothesis: cache invalidation/reload triggers synchronous blocking path in our runtime for some model variants.
2) Cost transparency mismatch: SDK + console compute tokenization and server-side token-count rounding differ; hypothesis: multiple tokenizers and post-processing steps (tool-calling wrappers) produce divergent counts.
3) Fallback behavior: model-variant polymorphism (e.g., ng1 -> ng2 variant mapping) leads to subtle tokenization/EOF differences; hypothesis: fallback variants are not fully ABI-compatible in tokenizer or special-token handling.

Compiled feature-requests (with quick notes on impact and candidate effort):
- Feature request A: "Streaming health headers / in-band signals" — a small protocol extension to emit explicit signals (cache-miss, model-variant-swap, degraded-latency) as structured events in the stream. Impact: high (reduces customer triage time). Effort: medium (runtime + SDK changes). Quick mitigation: return an easy-to-parse warning field in metadata until streaming headers are stable.

- Feature request B: "Transparent per-token billing breakdown API" — endpoint that returns both server token counts and a reconciled per-step billing summary. Impact: high for finance-facing customers. Effort: medium-high (billing + tokens pipeline + UI). Quick mitigation: publish a reconciliation doc + examples for common SDK usage patterns.

- Feature request C: "KV cache TTL/visibility dashboard and sample rehydration traces" — expose dashboard and per-request trace of cache state affecting latency. Impact: medium. Effort: low-medium (observability + UI change).

- Feature request D: "Failover compatibility matrix and safe-fallback policy" — document and/or config option that pins safe fallback pairs (model A -> model B) guaranteeing tokenizer/ABI compatibility. Impact: medium-high. Effort: low (docs + policy) to medium (runtime safeguard).

- Feature request E: "Private deploy KMS & audit quickstart" — one-pager + template scripts demonstrating KMS integration and audit log exports for on-prem/VPC installs. Impact: high for enterprise. Effort: low (docs and scripts).

Prioritization scaffold (suggested):
- Immediate (0–4 weeks): A (streaming health headers - prototype metadata), C (KV cache traces - add to existing tracing pipeline), E (KMS quickstart doc + checklist).
- Short (1–3 months): B (billing breakdown API - design + pilot), D (fallback compatibility matrix - policy + guard rails).

Acceptance criteria examples (for engineering handoff):
- Streaming health headers: SDKs (Python/Node) receive event types "cache_miss", "variant_swap" in-stream; unit tests that simulate cache rehydrate and assert event emission; integration smoke that shows timeline in console logs.
- KV cache traces: for any request id, console shows "cache_state" timeline with timestamps for: prefix-check, cache-hit/miss, rehydrate-start, rehydrate-end.
- KMS quickstart: runnable terraform script + README that sets up sample key + demo log export; tested on customer-simulated VPC.

Low-effort customer mitigations to ship now:
- Publish "billing reconciliation cheat-sheet" with tokenization examples for common SDK patterns (Node, Python).
- Add a short FAQ entry: "Why did my streaming suddenly slow down?" with steps to gather trace id and a recommended temporary throttle policy.
- Offer a concierge checklist to top-10 enterprise customers to validate KMS/audit readiness (CS-led).

Open questions & unresolved signals:
- Is there a measurable threshold of incoming prefix length distribution at which cache rehydration probability spikes? Need data query on prefix-length vs cache-miss rate.
- Are there model-specific tokenizer differences that make fallback mapping brittle? Need model onboarding team to confirm ABI compatibility matrix.
- How many customers rely on custom tool-calling wrappers that alter token counts? Suggest sampling 20 customers and comparing SDK logs to server-side counts.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing):
- Data spike: eng-observability to run prefix-length vs cache-miss query (owner: Evan Brooks) — due 2026-01-25.
- Prototype streaming metadata: serving-runtime + SDK (owner: Diego Alvarez) — POC by 2026-02-12.
- Billing reconciliation short doc: customer-success + finance (owner: Priya Nair) — publish 2026-01-28.
- KMS quickstart draft: solutions-eng + private-deployments (owner: Maya Chen) — publish 2026-02-05.

Appendix: small reproducible examples included in ticket set (refer to linked artifacts). Each example includes sample prompt, token counts seen client/server, trace id. Use these when running the POC.

Notes to reviewers: this is an initial synthesis intended to bridge CS signals with product/eng probes. Please comment inline with additional customer anecdotes, and flag anything that looks like an existing roadmap commitment so we avoid duplication.

-- end of memo --
